Hokay! Data engineering. Um. Spark notes. Software engineering but with data. Take Hinge. You have photos, prompts, messages, tied to a person. All of these profiles and their data need to be moved, stored, and retrieved/used. Data engineering is the process of setting up that whole 'pipeline'. 

So you have to think about the computational and storage needs. You need to make sure that updates propagate as quickly as they need to. And also make the data usable and available for feeding the matching algorithms and -then- take their results, and tie it back to the users with their best match predictions.

So, for data analysts to do their thing, they need...data! 🤣. At a small scale/company they go ahead and prepare their own. But at larger institutions where volume gets gnarly, that's when it makes sense to have dedicated roles for people that can build systems to collect, clean, and deliver data in a way that analysts can easily use. 😌

Thanks this app for instance. God knows how many are using it, and each person has a profile. The exchange messages, swipe left and right...all that data needs to be stored and organized for quick retrieval, and set up in a way for the matching algorithm to learn from you and present you with potential suitors.
